newsitem.title: GERMANY: Argentina's Menem courts investors on German visit.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem courts investors on German visit.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem, on a three-day state visit to Berlin and Bonn, on Tuesday called his country's relationship with Germany brotherly and said he looked forward to increasing German investment.

"Germany and Argentina are brother countries, both tirelessly working for the happiness of their citizens and the progress of their countries," Menem told reporters at the official opening of a new Argentine embassy in Berlin.
Menem met with German President Roman Herzog and Berlin Mayor Eberhardt Diepgen and laid a wreath at the city's memorial for victims of war and tyranny, the Neue Wache.
Menem told the mass circulation Bild newspaper in an interview one of the reasons why relations were so good was because around half a million Argentines had German ancestors.
"The ties between the two countries result from and grow mainly because of the people themselves," he said, adding that he thought it would be good if more Germans learned Spanish.

Menem said economic relations were also very strong and German firms currently had around $3 billion invested in his country. "And we do not doubt that that will continue to climb in the next few years," he told Bild.
Talks with Herzog dealt with expanding technological and economic ties between the two countries.

"We cannot afford to simply leave important areas of future technologies to the United States and Japan," Herzog said in a speech welcoming Menem late on Monday. "New areas of cooperation need to be developed."

Herzog added that he expected the large delegation of Argentine business leaders accompanying Menem would receive a warm welcome, considering the attractiveness of the Argentine economy for German companies.
He cited the double-digit growth rate in Argentina's automobile manufacturing industry as an example of economic conditions Germany could only dream of.
Menem continued on to Bonn on Tuesday afternoon, where he was set to dine with Chancellor Helmut Kohl. Menem is due to give a news conference in Bonn at 0815 GMT on Wednesday before flying to Cyprus.
